title: Brilliant Un-Pin
summary: Save the knight through checking moves, then answer two pins with concrete queen tactics.

nodes.question: Can White promote and keep the knight?
nodes.explanation: White has Kb5, Nf2 and pawns b7/f3 against Ke3, Rf4 and Bc1. Promotion alone allows the knight to fall.

branches.title: Let the knight go after the second pin
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece source root. The knight uses checks to survive until promotion.
Ng4+ checks e3 while offering the f3 pawn.
Kxf3 collects that pawn but allows a further knight check.
Ne5+ checks f3 and moves the knight out of immediate capture.
Ke4 is the selected king retreat.
b8=Q promotes. The new queen on b8 protects Ne5 along the diagonal.
Rf5 pins Ne5 to Kb5 along the fifth rank.
Kc4 steps off that rank. Capturing the knight now allows a queen fork of king and bishop.
Bf4 creates a relative pin: moving Ne5 would expose Qb8 to the bishop.
Qb7+ moves the queen off the bishop’s diagonal with check. White can now allow the king to take Ne5.
Kxe5 accepts the knight but places the king in the mating net.
Qe7# is actual mate. Kc4 covers d4/d5 while the queen and Black’s own bishop/rook close the other flights.
branches.explanation: Qe7# is actual mate. Kc4 covers d4/d5 while the queen and Black’s own bishop/rook close the other flights.

branches.title: Take the knight with the rook
commentary: Follow the source setup, then test the rook capture and illustrated king-bishop fork.
Ng4+ begins the checking route.
Kxf3 removes the sacrificed pawn.
Ne5+ checks while saving the knight.
Ke4 reaches the source’s central king square.
b8=Q promotes and protects Ne5.
Rf5 pins the knight to the king on b5.
Kc4 breaks the absolute pin and prepares the queen fork if the knight is taken.
Rxe5 wins the knight but exposes Ke4 and Bc1 to the queen fork.
Qb1+ checks Ke4 along the diagonal and attacks Bc1 along the first rank.
Kf3 is the illustrated king reply, stepping out of the queen’s diagonal.
Qxc1 wins the bishop. The remaining queen-versus-rook ending is checked as winning, rather than labeled immediate mate.
branches.explanation: Qxc1 wins the bishop. The remaining queen-versus-rook ending is checked as winning, rather than labeled immediate mate.

branches.title: Promote before saving the knight
commentary: Compare the source’s immediate promotion warning.
b8=Q promotes but gives up the forced win.
Kxf2 takes the knight. The exact queen-versus-rook-and-bishop position, including White’s f3 pawn, is drawn with best play; this endpoint is not an exhaustive proof of every fortress defense.

exercises.prompt: Why can White let the knight go at the end?
exercises.answer: After Qb7+ Kxe5, Qe7 is mate. The value of the knight is outweighed by the forcing mating net.
